etymologies.etymologyHTML: Borrowed from Latin fundus. Doublet of fond and fundus.

definitions.definition: A sum or source of money.
A money-management operation, such as a mutual fund.
A large supply of something to be drawn upon.

quote.citation: 1856 February, [Thomas Babington] Macaulay, “Oliver Goldsmith”, in T[homas] F[lower] E[llis], editor, The Miscellaneous Writings and Speeches of Lord Macaulay, new edition, London: Longman, Green, Reader, & Dyer, published 1871, →OCLC:
1945 January and February, A Former Pupil, “Some Memories of Crewe Works—III”, in Railway Magazine, page 14:
quote.text: He was a most likeable and generous man, a Whitworth Scholar, and possessed of a fund of knowledge which seemed to cover every subject under the sun.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To pay or provide money for.
(transitive) To form a debt into a stock charged with interest.
